```{r setup}
#| include: false

# load knitr 
library(knitr)

# set knitr chunk options 
opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,
                message = FALSE,
                warning = FALSE)
```

## Load Packages

```{r packages}

# load packages
library(openxlsx)
```

## Scramble Population 

```{r}

# read population file into data frame
population <- read.xlsx("../../data/raw/sampling/population.xlsx")

# set seed so the random row order is the same each time the script runs
set.seed(42)

# randomly reorder rows of dataframe
pop_scrambled <- population[sample(1:nrow(population)),]

```

## Export or Check Dataframe

The scrambled population is only written if the file does not exist yet. If it exists, the scramble reproduced here is checked against it, so knitting never overwrites the raw data.

```{r}

# path of the scrambled population in the raw sampling folder
scrambled_path <- "../../data/raw/sampling/population_scrambled.xlsx"

if (file.exists(scrambled_path)) {
  # check that the existing file matches the reproduced scramble, ignoring row names
  pop_scrambled_existing <- read.xlsx(scrambled_path)
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pop_scrambled_existing, pop_scrambled, check.attributes = FALSE)))
  cat("The existing population_scrambled.xlsx matches the reproduced scramble.\n")
} else {
  # write scrambled population in a new file
  write.xlsx(pop_scrambled, file = scrambled_path)
}

```
